regions.text: 偶然性が映げてるたとするならば織起偶然もまた成立し得ない。

quote.translation: If all the factors lacked any contingency of their own, no successive contingency could be constituted.

regions.text: 今の例で四といふ数をいつれの場合にもみな本人の故意で選んだとすれば、そこには最早や何等機起的偶然の生ずる除地のないのは云ふまでもないことである。

quote.translation: In the present example, if the person had deliberately chosen the number four on every occasion, there would, it goes without saying, no longer be any room for a successive contingency to arise.

regions.text: かやうな偶然性は單一者が同一性を以て数度縁返される點において「失はれし時を索めて」の著者プルウストをして云はしむれば「それらは現在と過去とに同時に存在し、現實的ではないが實在であり抽象的ではないが親念所である。

quote.translation: In that a single thing is repeated several times with identity, contingency of this kind is, to let Proust, the author of In Search of Lost Time, describe it, something of which one can say: "They exist simultaneously in the present and the past, not actual but real, not abstract but ideal ....

regions.text: ....時間の、秩席から解放された一利那が、時間の秩序から解放された人間を我等の中に再び造り出し、さうしてその利那を成覺させるのである』（MarcelProust，I

quote.translation: An instant (setsuna, 刹那) freed from the order of time creates again in us the human being freed from the order of time, and makes us feel that instant (setsuna, 刹那)" (Marcel Proust, Le Temps retrouvé, II, p. 16).

regions.text: eTempsretrouve,I.，p10）°この種の繼起偶然はに理由積極偶然の例として暴げた循壊小数112857,142957...や番數十入十八十入・・の姓名や一韻徹底i;jiiの押などの有つ偶然性（五九ー六三直照）が時間内に現象したものと云へるであらう。

quote.translation: Successive contingency of this kind may be said to be the contingency that we gave earlier as examples of positive contingency of ground (see pp. 59-63), the recurring decimal 142857, 142857 ..., personal names whose characters have eighteen, eighteen, eighteen ...

regions.text: （五九ー六三直照）が時間内に現象したものと云へるであら

quote.translation: strokes, or a rhyme held throughout on i, i, i, i, appearing within time.

regions.text: 藤蜜空蟬、ダ顔六條御息所紫上末摘花源典侍臘月夜内侍葵上、花散里明石上、齋宮女御朔顔玉意のすべてが光源氏にとつては同一性をもって繰返された幸ある偶然である。アルパノ湖昨の砂上にステッキで書いた十ニー

quote.translation: Fujitsubo, Utsusemi, Yūgao, the Rokujō Lady, Murasaki, Suetsumuhana, Gen no Naishi, Oborozukiyo no Naishi, Aoi, Hanachirusato, the Akashi Lady, the Saigū Consort, Asagao and Tamakazura are all, for Hikaru Genji, "happy chances" repeated with identity.

The twelve initials V, Aⁿ, Aᵈ, M, Mⁱ, Aˡ, Aⁱⁿᵉ, Aᵖᵍ, Mᵈᵉ, C, G, A that Stendhal wrote with his stick in the sand on the shore of Lake Albano are all, for him, "unhappy chances" repeated with identity.
